headword: {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}

definitions.explanation: A form of corporate management in which the founding family or their relatives hold controlling positions and ownership. Common in both small businesses and large corporations in Japan.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}だ。
{同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}には{良|よ}い{面|めん}も{悪|わる}い{面|めん}もある。
examples.english: Family management has both good and bad aspects.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{老舗|しにせ}には{同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}を{続|つづ}けている{企業|きぎょう}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Among Japan's long-established businesses, many continue as family-run enterprises.

notes:
A compound of {同族|どうぞく} (same clan/family) and {経営|けいえい} (management, business operation). Refers to businesses where the founding family retains control through ownership and key management positions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}の{会社|かいしゃ}: family-run company
- {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}を{続|つづ}ける: to continue family management
- {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}の{問題点|もんだいてん}: problems of family management
- {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}から{脱却|だっきゃく}する: to break away from family management

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many of Japan's largest corporations, including Toyota, Suntory, and numerous {老舗|しにせ} (long-established businesses), are or were {同族経営|どうぞくけいえい}. Japanese business culture has a strong tradition of family succession, though modern corporate governance reforms have pushed for more professional management.

RELATED WORDS:
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}: family-owned company — similar term focusing on ownership
- {家族経営|かぞくけいえい}: family-run — more for small businesses
- {世襲|せしゅう}: hereditary succession
- {老舗|しにせ}: long-established business
